title: Elevated Market Risk Alert
summary: Technical excess and coronavirus justify elevated risk.
coverage_note: All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

claims.reason: The exact RSI/MACD settings and chart interval are needed to reproduce the claim that conditions were the most extreme since January 2018. A later correction does not verify an indicator reading.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Business performance and shareholder return are distinct.
claims.next_check: Recompute source-chart RSI/MACD from the specified price series and lookback, including 2018 comparison.

claims.reason: Price momentum alone does not measure remaining buyers or establish causation. The author explicitly avoids claiming a certain next-week crash.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

claims.claim: China matters more globally than during SARS
claims.reason: The proposition requires comparable GDP, trade and travel shares for 2003 and 2020. The mechanism is plausible but those denominators have not been verified.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.
claims.next_check: Compare World Bank GDP/trade shares and outbound travel using same definitions.

claims.reason: Subsequent CDC investigation documented likely presymptomatic transmission and explained the containment challenge. This supports the qualitative concern, not every early incubation estimate.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.title: Presymptomatic transmission in Singapore
evidence.finding: Investigation identified seven clusters consistent with presymptomatic transmission; in four clusters exposure occurred one to three days before source-patient symptoms. This created containment difficulties.

claims.claim: China disruption spills into global growth
claims.reason: The later global pandemic and US contraction confirm economic damage, but they do not isolate spillovers from China from domestic outbreaks. The original China-only pathway needs separate evidence.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Travel and production disruption supported; China-only attribution unresolved.

evidence.title: First-quarter 2020 GDP advance estimate
evidence.finding: Initial Q1 real GDP estimate was -4.8% annualized. BEA linked the decline partly to pandemic responses, with lower services and travel exports, while warning the complete COVID effect could not be isolated.

claims.claim: Past-outbreak pattern could mean temporary disruption
claims.reason: The benign outcome was conditional on a past-outbreak-like course. The worldwide pandemic violated that trigger; the scenario is neither an unconditional miss nor a forecast win.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.
claims.next_check: Do not score as a realized branch; compare explicit later revisions when containment fails.

claims.claim: A severe outbreak remains a tail risk
claims.reason: A severe pandemic and substantial economic interruption occurred. Credit this as identifying a material risk, not as an accurate numerical probability or magnitude forecast.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

claims.claim: Monday is likely to gap lower
claims.reason: The S&P 500 opened January 27, 2020 at 3247.16, below the January 24 close of 3295.47, a 1.47% opening gap. This verifies the explicit next-session directional forecast, separately from the later pandemic crash.
claims.direction_assessment: See independently checked outcomes and qualifications in reason.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.title: S&P 500 historical OHLC
evidence.finding: January 27, 2020 open 3247.16; prior January 24 close 3295.47; opening gap -1.47%.

framework_lessons: Combine positioning with a plausible shock.
assessment: This was a timely warning about a material emerging risk. It did not predict the full pandemic path or a certain immediate crash, and should not be credited retrospectively with either. The next-day gap call is unusually testable but awaits a verified opening-price source.
verification_limitations: Retrieved 2026-11-07; publication-date wording is not authenticated.
No complete adjusted total-return series or original-vintage macro database was available for this review. Unverified outcomes are explicitly unscored.
